sources.README.md:
# Library sound restoration upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Ruby 2.7.0p0.
Dependencies: Ruby standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

# Preservation sessions use block observers and distinct Struct visits.
Visit=Struct.new(:id,:file,:handle)
module Cancellation
 def cancel
  return if @aborted
  @aborted=true;@stop.call;@env.call('cancel',@file['token'],@number)
 end
end
class Attempt
 include Cancellation
 attr_reader :file,:number,:aborted
 def initialize(env,file,number,active=-> {1},audit=->(f){},view=->(f,o){})
  @env,@file,@number,@aborted=env,file,number,false;@stop=->{};env.call('transport',file['token'],number)
  if file['feed']
   callback=env.bind(->(packet){
    order=active.call;
    deliver=->(frame){ audit.call(frame);view.call(frame,order)}
    value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']
   })
   env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
   @stop=-> {env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription)};@stop.call if @aborted
  end
 end
end
class Session
 def initialize(env);@env=env;@visit=nil;@serial=0;@attempts=0;@tasks={};@disposed=false;end
 def current(v);@visit.equal?(v);end
 def enqueue(v,kind)
  @attempts+=1;n=@attempts;entry={fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,visitId:v.id,kind:kind};;@env.call('record',entry)
  h=Attempt.new(@env,v.file,n,->{0},->(frame){@env.call('recordProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame})},->(frame,order){@env.call('showProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame}) if current(v)});@tasks[n]=h;h
 end
 def notice(v,h);;@env.call('showQueued',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:h.number,visitId:v.id,status:'queued'});end
 def release(v);h=v.handle;v.handle=nil;h.cancel if h;end
 def select(file)
  return nil if @disposed
  @serial+=1;request=@serial;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old
  return nil if @disposed||@serial!=request
  v=Visit.new(request,file,nil);@visit=v;h=enqueue(v,'select');if current(v);v.handle=h;notice(v,h);else;h.cancel;end;h
 end
 def retry
  v=@visit;return nil if !v||!v.handle||@disposed
  v.handle.cancel
  accepted=v;h=enqueue(accepted,'retry');if current(accepted);accepted.handle=h;else;h.cancel;end;notice(accepted,h) if current(accepted);h
 end
 def hide;@serial+=1;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old;end
 def dispose;return if @disposed;@disposed=true;hide;@tasks.each_value(&:cancel);end
 def snapshot;v=@visit;{visitId:v ? v.id : nil,fileId:v ? v.file['id'] : nil,attemptId:v&&v.handle ? v.handle.number : nil,disposed:@disposed,attempts:@attempts};end
end

class Telemetry
 attr_reader :stop
 def initialize(env,file)
  callback=env.bind(->(packet){deliver=->(frame){env.call('recordDelta',frame)};value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']})
  env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
  @stop=->{env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription)}
 end
end

rules.body:
Apply when progress reception serves distinct visits and physical attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding may finish later, and audit and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." README.md: "The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order." Confirm these premises before transferring this guidance.

Install panel reception before starting the source, while preserving subsequent streaming and source reuse. Original src/workflow.rb: "env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)". Guard admission using the originating subscription and visit, including during startup before the outer caller receives its handle. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle." Retirement must prevent subsequent admission without relying solely on eventual physical cleanup.

Where the task explicitly requires protection against out-of-order full frames, capture reception order before decoding and retain a publication watermark for the visit, spanning its retries. Publish an eligible completion only if it cannot replace a newer frame already displayed. Commit the watermark before invoking callback-capable presentation so reentrant publication cannot restore older authority. TASK: "Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward." Compare reception order rather than numeric progress: README.md states, "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Continue auditing suppressed older completions.

Bind accepted decoding to its originating file, attempt and visit. Preserve its audit effect when decoding completes, including after cancellation or retirement, then recheck visit eligibility before visible publication. Original src/workflow.rb: "deliver=->(frame){ audit.call(frame);view.call(frame,order)}" and "->(frame,order){@env.call('showProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame}) if current(v)}". README.md: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." Because audit callbacks may navigate synchronously, an admission-time validity check cannot replace the publication-time check. Already accepted decoding is not automatically ineligible for display solely because retry canceled its attempt while the visit remains current.

Establish cleanup ownership before callback-capable startup, remove captured old ownership before cancellation, and recheck authority after callbacks. An older startup must clean its own retired resources without overwriting newer navigation. Original src/workflow.rb: "@serial+=1;request=@serial;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old\n  return nil if @disposed||@serial!=request". Preserve removal commitment and idempotence: README.md states, "Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;\nthat callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is\ninert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred." Keep cancellation and disposal independent for each workspace.

Keep an accepted retry bound to its entry visit across cancellation callbacks. Cancel the prior handle before enqueueing; preserve its one queue record and transfer construction even if cancellation navigates; cancel the resulting transfer if its visit ended and suppress retired queued notices. Original src/workflow.rb: "v.handle.cancel\n  accepted=v;h=enqueue(accepted,'retry');if current(accepted);accepted.handle=h;else;h.cancel;end;notice(accepted,h) if current(accepted);h". Preserve queue recording before transfer construction and existing counters. Original src/workflow.rb: "@attempts+=1;n=@attempts;entry={fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,visitId:v.id,kind:kind};;@env.call('record',entry)".

Keep freshness filtering specific to the panel requirement; do not transfer it to unrelated consumers or tasks without supporting evidence. Preserve public queue and notice fields and adapter interfaces. README.md: "Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}\nunless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size." No separate authorization is supplied. Preserve diagnostic behavior, including its existing startup sequence: README.md states, "The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/\ncollectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate\nfrom the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance."

Verify freshness across retries and reentrant publication, including navigation during recordProgress. checkpoints: A warm source's synchronously emitted cached packet is received by the panel and produces the initial progress update.
Packets emitted later through the same panel subscription continue to decode, audit, and display normally.
When a later-received frame is displayed before an earlier-received frame finishes decoding, the earlier frame is still audited but does not replace the display.
A later-received frame whose loaded value is lower or reset may still replace the display.
Freshness ordering spans retry attempts within the same visit, while selecting the same file again creates a new ordering lifetime.
Navigation or disposal during synchronous startup prevents the retired visit from admitting subsequent startup packets; any already admitted decode retains its audit effect.
Navigation reentered from showProgress, unlisten, or cancellation does not let an older operation overwrite the newer visit or its resources.

An accepted retry remains associated with its entry visit, retains its queue record, cancels its resulting attempt if that visit has ended, and emits a queued notice only if the visit is still current.
Repeated cancellation, listener removal, and disposal remain inert after their first effective action.
Telemetry retains its existing start-before-listen sequence and live delta behavior.
Queue records and queued notices retain their existing fields, and record remains before transfer construction.
Ruby public syntax is checked after any Action; this check is not treated as proof of business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not change public transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, cancellation, notice, or queue-record behavior beyond coordination necessary for the panel repair.
Do not add byteCount or any other field to queue records.
Do not suppress recordProgress for an admitted decode merely because its frame is no longer eligible for display.
Do not use loaded magnitude as the freshness rule; loaded values may legitimately decrease or reset.
Do not apply the panel's initial-frame or full-frame freshness policy to Telemetry.
Do not allow retired subscriptions to admit new decoding during callback-capable startup.
Do not allow an older startup, listener-removal callback, or cancellation callback to replace or cancel resources owned by newer navigation.
Do not treat physical cancellation or listener removal as retracting decoding that was already admitted.
Do not merge separate workspaces' lifecycle, attempt counters, visits, or display watermarks.
lifecycle_identity: A visit is created by selection; retry replaces the physical attempt while retaining that visit.
Selecting the same file object again creates a distinct visit even though the file and source are shared.
An admitted packet is associated with its originating file, physical attempt, visit, and reception order.
Display freshness belongs to the visit and therefore spans retries in that visit; a newly selected visit has a distinct freshness lifetime.
Attempt numbering and workspace disposal state remain local to each Session instance.
The current visit is determined by object identity through Session#current, not merely by file id.

obligations.text: The panel must establish progress reception before starting a warm source so cached packets emitted synchronously by start can produce the initial progress update, while preserving reception of later packets.
Each packet admitted by the originating live visit must be assigned reception order before decoding, because decoding may complete immediately or on a later host turn.
Every admitted decode completion must retain its existing recordProgress audit effect exactly once, including when its visit or attempt has since been retired.
After auditing, a decoded full frame may be shown only if its originating visit is still current and no newer-received frame has already been published for that visit.

The publication watermark must advance before showProgress is invoked, and authority and freshness must be rechecked after recordProgress, because host callbacks may synchronously navigate or deliver other progress.

Logical retirement must immediately stop a subscription from admitting further packets, including additional synchronous packets emitted before startup returns and before physical unlisten is available.
Startup and cleanup ownership must be reconciled so a handle returned after its visit was retired is cleaned up without overwriting resources installed by newer navigation.

Retry must preserve its existing entry-visit semantics: cancel the previous attempt, enqueue and record the accepted retry once, retain the new handle only if that visit remains current, otherwise cancel it, and publish its queued notice only while current.
Queue recording, transport construction, cancellation order, payload shapes, per-session counters, idempotent cleanup, and subsequent source reuse must remain observably unchanged.
Telemetry must retain its existing diagnostic behavior and must not inherit the panel's bootstrap reception or freshness filtering changes.

ordering_barriers: For the panel, listener registration must occur before the callback-capable start call.
Packet reception order must be captured before decode begins.
recordProgress must occur before the decision and action to showProgress.
After recordProgress returns, current-visit authority and the publication watermark must be checked again.
The publication watermark must be committed before invoking showProgress.
A retiring visit must lose logical admission authority before callback-capable unlisten or cancellation runs.
Older ownership must be detached from current session state before cleanup callbacks can reenter navigation.
Queue record creation must remain before Attempt construction and transport startup.
Retry cancellation of the previous handle must remain before enqueueing the accepted retry.
Attempt cancellation must preserve stop/unlisten before the environment cancel notification.
preservation: Ordinary later streaming through the panel subscription remains active.
recordProgress continues to append history for every admitted decoded frame even if presentation is suppressed.
Existing transfer creation, retry acceptance, visit navigation, disposal, and cleanup behavior remains intact.
The existing queue record is exactly {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}.
The existing queued notice remains {fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: 'queued'}.
The same file and source remain reusable by later visits and attempts.
Cancellation and listener removal remain idempotent.
Telemetry continues to observe its existing live decoded deltas with its existing startup ordering.
Each workspace retains an independent lifetime and attempt counter.
A newer-received frame may legitimately show a lower or reset loaded value.
scope: Business behavior in src/workflow.rb for panel progress setup, admission, decode completion, display freshness, and the lifecycle coordination required to preserve Session behavior.
The panel path created by Session#enqueue and Attempt, including synchronous start, later streaming, immediate decode, and deferred decode completion.
Existing Session selection, retry, hiding, disposal, cancellation, ownership, audit, notice, and queue-record behavior insofar as it must be preserved.
Telemetry is in preservation scope only: its behavior must remain unchanged.
No tests, configuration, dependency metadata, scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests are in scope.

# Library sound restoration upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Ruby 2.7.0p0.
Dependencies: Ruby standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

module Cancellation
 def cancel
  return if @aborted
  @aborted=true;@stop.call;@env.call('cancel',@file['token'],@number)
 end
end
class Attempt
 include Cancellation
 attr_reader :file,:number,:aborted
 def initialize(env,file,number,active=-> {1},audit=->(f){},view=->(f,o){})
  @env,@file,@number,@aborted=env,file,number,false;@stop=->{};env.call('transport',file['token'],number)
  yield self if block_given?
  if file['feed']
   callback=env.bind(->(packet){
    next if @aborted
    order=active.call;
    next if order.nil?||@aborted
    deliver=->(frame){ audit.call(frame);view.call(frame,order)}
    value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']
   })
   subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
   @stop=-> {env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription)}
   if @aborted;@stop.call;else;env.call('start',file['token']);end
  end
 end
end
class Session
 def initialize(env);@env=env;@visit=nil;@serial=0;@attempts=0;@tasks={};@progress={}.compare_by_identity;@disposed=false;end
 def current(v);@visit.equal?(v);end
 def admit(v)
  return nil unless current(v)
  state=@progress[v];state[:received]+=1
 end
 def publish(v,order)
  return false unless current(v)
  state=@progress[v];return false if order<=state[:published]
  state[:published]=order;true
 end
 def enqueue(v,kind)
  @attempts+=1;n=@attempts;entry={fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,visitId:v.id,kind:kind};;@env.call('record',entry)
  h=Attempt.new(@env,v.file,n,->{admit(v)},->(frame){@env.call('recordProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame})},->(frame,order){@env.call('showProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame}) if publish(v,order)}){|attempt|v.handle=attempt if current(v)};@tasks[n]=h;h
 end
 def notice(v,h);;@env.call('showQueued',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:h.number,visitId:v.id,status:'queued'});end
 def release(v);h=v.handle;v.handle=nil;h.cancel if h;end
 def select(file)
  return nil if @disposed
  @serial+=1;request=@serial;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old
  return nil if @disposed||@serial!=request
  v=Visit.new(request,file,nil);@progress[v]={received:0,published:0};@visit=v;h=enqueue(v,'select');if current(v)&&v.handle.equal?(h);notice(v,h);else;h.cancel;end;h
 end
 def retry
  v=@visit;return nil if !v||!v.handle||@disposed
  v.handle.cancel
  accepted=v;h=enqueue(accepted,'retry');if current(accepted)&&accepted.handle.equal?(h);notice(accepted,h);else;h.cancel;end;h
 end
 def hide;@serial+=1;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old;end
 def dispose;return if @disposed;@disposed=true;hide;@tasks.each_value(&:cancel);end
 def snapshot;v=@visit;{visitId:v ? v.id : nil,fileId:v ? v.file['id'] : nil,attemptId:v&&v.handle ? v.handle.number : nil,disposed:@disposed,attempts:@attempts};end
end
